effect: Calcium (especially from supplements or dairy) significantly reduces non-heme iron absorption when taken together
management: Take iron supplements 2 hours before or after calcium supplements or dairy

effect: High doses of zinc reduce iron absorption. High doses of iron reduce zinc absorption.
management: Take zinc and iron supplements at different times of day. Do not take high doses of both simultaneously.

effect: High zinc intake (>40mg/day) depletes copper stores over time, causing copper deficiency anemia and neurological issues
management: If taking zinc supplements >25mg/day, also supplement 1-2mg copper per 15mg zinc

effect: Vitamin D is essential for calcium absorption. Without adequate vitamin D, calcium from food and supplements is poorly absorbed.
management: Take together for best effect. Most calcium supplements now include vitamin D3.

effect: Vitamin C converts non-heme iron to a more absorbable form, increasing absorption up to 3-fold
management: Take vitamin C alongside iron-rich foods or supplements to maximize absorption

effect: High calcium intake can reduce magnesium absorption. Ideal calcium:magnesium ratio is 2:1.
management: Balance calcium and magnesium intake. Take at different times if taking large supplement doses.

effect: Vitamin D increases calcium absorption, vitamin K2 directs calcium to bones. Both needed for bone health and to prevent arterial calcification.
management: Take vitamin D3 with vitamin K2 (MK-7 form) for optimal bone and cardiovascular benefit

effect: Fat-soluble vitamins absorb better when taken with dietary fat. Fish oil provides the fat needed for absorption.
management: Take vitamins A, D, E, K with a meal containing fat or with fish oil capsules

effect: Iron and vitamin E can oxidize each other when taken together, reducing the effectiveness of both
management: Take iron and vitamin E at least 4 hours apart

effect: Very high folate intake may reduce zinc absorption
management: Avoid taking very high folic acid doses (>1mg/day) with zinc supplements

effect: Large doses of calcium inhibit magnesium absorption by competing for the same transporters
management: Take calcium and magnesium at different times if taking high doses of both

effect: B12 and folate work together in methylation. Deficiency of one masks deficiency of the other and both are needed for RBC formation.
management: Take together. Especially important in pregnancy to prevent neural tube defects.
